text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister Majali holds talks in Tunis on bilateral cooperation and Middle East peace process.
- Military court hears that Private Ahmed Daqamsa, accused killer of Israeli schoolgirls, has a personality disorder.
- Approval for nearly 10,000 Jordanian claims of compensation over 1990-1991 Gulf War.
- Detainees from last Sunday's violence in Deir Alla freed. Majali to go to Deir Alla next week to discuss grievances after security forces destroyed houses built on government land.

- Justice Minister Shakaa says government taking Al-Arab Al-Yawm newspaper to court over front-page article which said over 50 infiltrators had been caught in Jordan planning attacks. First case to go to courts under new press law.
- Parliamentary speaker Srour says Israeli Knesset vote to join Jewish settlements in West Bank and Gaza to Israel is decision to handicap peace process.
- Cabinet expected to decide on Saturday to activate investment company as part of Aqaba free trade zone project.
- Jordan's Housing Bank expected to announce next week plans to double capital to 50 million dinars ($70 million) after receiving promises of support for a share issue from Gulf Arab investors.
- Economic and investment deal expected soon between Jordan and EFTA states.
- Prime Minister Majali arrives in Tunis.
